newsitem.title: USA: InVitro to merge with Shenyang.
newsitem.headline: InVitro to merge with Shenyang.

text.p: InVitro International said it signed a letter of intent to merge with Shenyang International Inc in a deal in which InVitro stockholders would retain 20 percent of the combined company's common stock.

InVitro expects the proposal will be presented to InVitro's board before the end of March 1997. ShenYang owns 99 percent of ShenYang Holding Co and operates four business divisions in mainland China with 300 employees.
ShenYang Holding has operated profitably for the last five years, and its annual revenues have risen from $6.5 million in 1992 to more than $15 million currently, InVitro said.

Assuming the proposed merger were successfully completed, InVitro said it would undertake to reduce its existing business operations to eliminate negative cash flow and currently anticipates those operations will continue under the direction of InVitro's management as a separate division or subsidiary of the combined enterprise.
